osces.title: Hypertrophic Cardiomyopathy - Exercise Restriction Counseling

patient_scenario.chief_complaint: Referred after abnormal sports screening ECG, requesting clearance to continue competitive swimming
patient_scenario.history_presenting_illness: Asymptomatic 19-year-old competitive swimmer referred after mandatory sports screening revealed abnormal ECG. Trains 15 hours per week, competes at state level. No exertional symptoms - no chest pain, palpitations, or syncope. However, on direct questioning admits to occasional light-headedness after rapid standing, particularly after training sessions. Elder brother died suddenly age 22 while playing basketball - cause listed as 'cardiac arrest'. Father has 'thick heart muscle' diagnosed age 45.

social_history.exercise: Elite athlete - swimming training 15 hours/week, gym 3 hours/week
social_history.occupation_detail: Second year sports science student, aspiring for Olympic trials

patient_scenario.family_history: Brother died suddenly age 22 during basketball (cardiac arrest), father diagnosed with HCM age 45, paternal grandfather died suddenly age 51 'heart attack'

examination_findings.cardiovascular: JVP not elevated. Apex beat forceful, not displaced. Grade 3/6 ejection systolic murmur at left sternal edge, increases with Valsalva manoeuvre and standing, decreases with squatting. Loud S4 gallop. Bifid carotid pulse palpable. Peripheral pulses normal.
examination_findings.respiratory: Clear lung fields bilaterally, no crackles or wheeze
examination_findings.other_systems: Abdomen soft, non-tender. No peripheral oedema. Athletic build, BMI 23

investigations.ecg: Sinus bradycardia 52 bpm, PR interval 160ms, QRS 98ms. Voltage criteria for LVH (SV1 + RV5 = 42mm). Deep T wave inversions V3-V6. Abnormal Q waves in inferior and lateral leads. No delta waves.
investigations.chest_xray: Normal cardiac silhouette, clear lung fields, no pulmonary congestion
investigations.bloods: FBC normal, UEC normal, Troponin I <2 ng/L (normal), BNP 25 pg/mL (normal)
investigations.echocardiogram: Asymmetric septal hypertrophy, interventricular septum 22mm (normal <12mm), posterior wall 11mm. Systolic anterior motion of mitral valve with mitral-septal contact. LVOT gradient 45mmHg at rest, increases to 90mmHg with Valsalva. Ejection fraction 70%. LA diameter 38mm.
investigations.other: 24-hour Holter: 3 runs of non-sustained VT (4-6 beats) at rates 150-170 bpm. Exercise stress test: appropriate BP response, no symptoms, NSVT 5 beats at peak exercise

immediate: Cease all competitive sports immediately pending further evaluation
Urgent cardiology referral for risk stratification
short_term: Cardiac MRI for tissue characterisation and fibrosis assessment
Genetic testing for sarcomeric mutations
Family screening - ECG and echo for all first-degree relatives
long_term: ICD consideration given family history and NSVT on monitoring
Lifelong restriction from competitive sports per CSANZ guidelines
Annual cardiology follow-up with echo and Holter monitoring
Genetic counselling for family planning
discharge_planning: Written advice regarding exercise restrictions
Emergency action plan for syncope or cardiac symptoms
MedicAlert bracelet for HCM diagnosis
Psychology referral for adjustment to sports restriction

marking_criteria.item: Recognises systolic murmur increases with Valsalva/standing
Identifies high-risk family history (SCD in brother)
Correctly interprets echo findings of HCM with LVOT obstruction
Recommends immediate cessation of competitive sports
Initiates beta-blocker therapy for symptom control
Orders appropriate investigations (echo, Holter, cardiac MRI)
Arranges family screening for first-degree relatives
Discusses ICD indication given NSVT and family history
Provides appropriate exercise counselling (recreational only)
Addresses psychological impact of sports restriction

learning_objectives: Recognise clinical features of hypertrophic cardiomyopathy including dynamic LVOT obstruction
Apply CSANZ guidelines for exercise restriction in HCM patients
Identify high-risk features for sudden cardiac death in HCM
Understand importance of family screening in inherited cardiac conditions
references: CSANZ Guidelines for the diagnosis and management of hypertrophic cardiomyopathy 2021
National Heart Foundation position statement on screening young athletes

osces.title: Dilated Cardiomyopathy - Heart Failure Medication Optimization

patient_scenario.chief_complaint: Worsening breathlessness and ankle swelling over 3 weeks despite current heart failure medications
patient_scenario.history_presenting_illness: Known dilated cardiomyopathy diagnosed 18 months ago, initially presenting with acute pulmonary oedema. LVEF 25% on last echo 6 months ago. Progressive dyspnoea over 3 weeks, now NYHA class III (previously class II). Cannot walk to letterbox without stopping. Sleeping with 3 pillows, waking twice nightly with breathlessness. Bilateral ankle oedema to mid-shin. Weight gain 5kg in 2 weeks. Taking medications regularly but admits to dietary indiscretion at recent family gatherings. No chest pain, palpitations or syncope.

social_history.exercise: Limited by dyspnoea, walks 50 metres maximum
social_history.occupation_detail: Retired teacher, lives with supportive husband

patient_scenario.family_history: Mother died heart failure age 78, father stroke age 72, no family history of cardiomyopathy

examination_findings.cardiovascular: JVP elevated 8cm above sternal angle. Displaced apex beat 6th intercostal space anterior axillary line. Soft S1, normal S2, loud S3 gallop. Grade 2/6 pansystolic murmur at apex radiating to axilla. Bilateral pitting oedema to knees.
examination_findings.respiratory: Bibasal fine inspiratory crackles to mid-zones bilaterally. No wheeze.
examination_findings.other_systems: Abdomen distended, shifting dullness present (ascites). Tender hepatomegaly 3cm below costal margin.

investigations.ecg: Sinus rhythm 68 bpm, PR 180ms, LBBB pattern QRS 140ms, no acute ischaemic changes
investigations.chest_xray: Cardiomegaly (CTR 0.65), upper lobe blood diversion, bilateral pleural effusions (right > left), Kerley B lines
investigations.bloods: Na 134 mmol/L, K 4.2 mmol/L, Cr 115 μmol/L (eGFR 48), Urea 9.2 mmol/L, BNP 1850 pg/mL (markedly elevated), Hb 118 g/L, Albumin 32 g/L, ALT 45 U/L, Bilirubin 28 μmol/L
investigations.echocardiogram: Previous echo: Dilated LV (LVEDD 68mm), severe global hypokinesis, LVEF 25%, moderate MR, moderate TR, RVSP 45mmHg, no LV thrombus
investigations.other: Recent angiography (6 months ago): Normal coronary arteries, confirming non-ischaemic cardiomyopathy

immediate: Increase frusemide to 80mg BD for diuresis - PBS code 1737B
Add spironolactone 12.5mg daily (start low given eGFR) - PBS code 1948W
Daily weights and strict fluid restriction 1.5L/day
short_term: Stop perindopril today, 36-hour washout period
Start sacubitril-valsartan (Entresto) 24/26mg BD after washout - PBS code 11766L (authority required)
Uptitrate bisoprolol to 3.75mg daily once euvolaemic
Check UEC and BNP in 3 days
long_term: Gradual uptitration of Entresto to target 97/103mg BD over 6 weeks
Uptitrate bisoprolol to maximum tolerated dose (target 10mg daily)
CRT-D assessment given LBBB with QRS >130ms and LVEF <35%
Heart failure nurse specialist follow-up
Consider SGLT2 inhibitor (empagliflozin) for additional benefit
discharge_planning: Discharge when 3kg weight loss achieved and symptoms improved
Heart failure action plan with daily weights
Dietitian review for 2g sodium diet education
Outpatient clinic 1 week post-discharge

marking_criteria.item: Recognises volume overload requiring increased diuresis
Correctly initiates spironolactone for mortality benefit
Plans appropriate ACE-I to ARNI switch with washout period
Identifies need for beta-blocker uptitration once stable
Monitors potassium and renal function with new medications
Recognises CRT-D indication (LBBB, QRS >130ms, LVEF <35%)
Implements fluid restriction and daily weights
Arranges appropriate multidisciplinary follow-up
Considers SGLT2 inhibitor for additional benefit
Provides patient education and heart failure action plan

learning_objectives: Apply guideline-directed medical therapy sequencing in HFrEF
Understand appropriate transition from ACE-I to ARNI therapy
Recognise indications for device therapy (CRT-D) in heart failure
Implement comprehensive heart failure management including lifestyle measures
references: CSANZ 2022 Guidelines for the Prevention, Detection and Management of Heart Failure
National Heart Foundation Guidelines for the management of heart failure 2023

osces.title: Complete Heart Block - Temporary vs Permanent Pacing Decision

patient_scenario.chief_complaint: Found collapsed at home by wife, now bradycardic and confused in emergency department
patient_scenario.history_presenting_illness: Brought in by ambulance after wife found him collapsed in bathroom 2 hours ago. Brief loss of consciousness, no seizure activity witnessed. Confused on waking, complained of dizziness and nausea. Paramedics documented heart rate 28 bpm. In ED, remains dizzy when sitting up, nauseated, mild central chest heaviness. Wife reports 3 similar but less severe dizzy spells over past week, each lasting seconds. No recent medication changes. Background of inferior STEMI 8 years ago treated with PCI to RCA.
past_medical_history: Inferior STEMI 2018 - PCI to RCA with drug-eluting stent

social_history.occupation_detail: Retired electrician, lives with wife, independent with ADLs

patient_scenario.family_history: Father died MI age 68, mother stroke age 82, no family history of conduction disease

examination_findings.cardiovascular: JVP visible with cannon A waves. Regular bradycardia, variable intensity S1. No murmurs. Cool peripheries, capillary refill 4 seconds. Peripheral pulses palpable but weak.
examination_findings.respiratory: Clear lung fields, no crackles or wheeze
examination_findings.other_systems: Alert but slow to respond, GCS 15. Abdomen soft non-tender. No focal neurology.

investigations.ecg: Complete heart block. Ventricular rate 32 bpm, regular. P waves 75 bpm, regular. Complete AV dissociation with P waves marching through QRS complexes. QRS duration 140ms with RBBB morphology (escape from left bundle). No acute ST changes.
investigations.chest_xray: Normal heart size, clear lungs, permanent pacing lead from previous temporary wire visible in RV apex (fractured)
investigations.bloods: Troponin I 85 ng/L (mildly elevated), K 5.1 mmol/L, Na 138 mmol/L, Cr 125 μmol/L, Urea 7.8 mmol/L, Mg 0.82 mmol/L, Corrected Ca 2.35 mmol/L, TSH 2.1 mU/L
investigations.echocardiogram: Bedside echo: Normal LV function (EF 55%), inferior wall hypokinesis (old), no acute wall motion abnormality, no pericardial effusion
investigations.other: Previous angiogram (2018): RCA stent patent, 30% LAD stenosis, 40% Cx stenosis

immediate: Atropine 600mcg IV - ineffective (expected in complete heart block)
Urgent temporary pacing wire insertion via right internal jugular approach
Transcutaneous pacing pads as backup while preparing for transvenous wire
short_term: Continuous cardiac monitoring in CCU
Serial troponins to exclude acute ischaemia
Urgent cardiology review for permanent pacemaker
Check pacing thresholds twice daily
long_term: Permanent dual-chamber pacemaker insertion within 24-48 hours
Consider ICD given previous MI and moderate LV dysfunction
Pacemaker clinic follow-up at 1 week, then 3 monthly
May need to restart beta-blocker at lower dose post-PPM
discharge_planning: Discharge day 2 post-permanent pacemaker insertion
Pacemaker identification card and MedicAlert bracelet
Driving restrictions 2 weeks private, 4 weeks commercial license
Wound care instructions and signs of infection education

marking_criteria.item: Correctly identifies complete heart block on ECG
Recognises atropine ineffectiveness in complete heart block
Appropriately withholds beta-blocker
Arranges urgent temporary pacing (transcutaneous or transvenous)
Correctly identifies right internal jugular as preferred access
Plans permanent pacemaker within appropriate timeframe
Chooses dual-chamber over single-chamber pacemaker
Monitors for complications (lead displacement, pneumothorax)
Provides appropriate driving restriction advice
Arranges appropriate follow-up and device monitoring

learning_objectives: Recognise ECG features of complete heart block with AV dissociation
Understand indications for temporary vs permanent cardiac pacing
Apply Australian driving guidelines following pacemaker insertion
Manage haemodynamic compromise from bradyarrhythmias
references: eTG - Cardiovascular: Cardiac arrhythmias and pacing
Austroads guidelines for fitness to drive - cardiac conditions

osces.title: Wolff-Parkinson-White Syndrome - Medication Safety in Pre-Excitation

patient_scenario.chief_complaint: Recurrent palpitations with near-syncope, ECG shows pre-excitation pattern
patient_scenario.history_presenting_illness: ED nurse self-presented after episode of rapid palpitations during night shift 3 hours ago. Heart rate felt >200 bpm, associated with chest tightness, dizziness and pre-syncope. Symptoms lasted 20 minutes, terminated spontaneously after vagal manoeuvres. Three similar episodes over past 6 months, each lasting 5-30 minutes. Previous episodes terminated with Valsalva or cold water immersion. No syncope but feels 'about to faint' during episodes. Between episodes completely asymptomatic. Concerned about episodes occurring while caring for critically ill patients.

social_history.exercise: Gym 3 times per week, runs 5km twice weekly
social_history.occupation_detail: Senior ED nurse, rotating shifts, high-stress environment

patient_scenario.family_history: Nil cardiac history, mother has migraines, father hypertensive

examination_findings.cardiovascular: JVP not elevated. Normal apex beat. Normal S1 S2, no murmurs or added sounds. No carotid bruits. Peripheral pulses normal and equal.
examination_findings.other_systems: Alert and oriented. No thyromegaly. Neurologically intact.

investigations.ecg: Sinus rhythm 68 bpm, PR interval 100ms (short), QRS 124ms with delta wave (slurred upstroke) best seen in V4-V6, secondary repolarisation abnormalities. Type B pattern (negative delta V1, positive V2-V6) suggesting right-sided pathway.
investigations.chest_xray: Normal cardiac size and contour, clear lung fields
investigations.bloods: FBC normal, UEC normal, TSH 1.8 mU/L, Troponin I <2 ng/L
investigations.echocardiogram: Structurally normal heart, LVEF 60%, no valvular abnormalities, no evidence of cardiomyopathy or Ebstein's anomaly
investigations.other: 24-hour Holter (arranged urgently): Baseline pre-excitation, one episode of narrow complex tachycardia rate 210 bpm lasting 8 minutes (orthodromic AVRT), self-terminated

immediate: Education on vagal manoeuvres for episode termination
Strict avoidance of AV nodal blockers - document allergy alert
Provide written list of contraindicated medications
If presents with AF: NO digoxin, verapamil, diltiazem (risk of VF)
short_term: Urgent electrophysiology referral for risk stratification
Consider flecainide 100mg BD as bridge to ablation - PBS code 1750N
Workplace risk assessment given patient-care responsibilities
Holter monitoring to document arrhythmia burden
long_term: Catheter ablation of accessory pathway (curative in >95%)
Pre-ablation counselling: 0.5% major complication risk
Return to full duties 48 hours post-successful ablation
No long-term medication required if ablation successful
discharge_planning: MedicAlert bracelet stating WPW - avoid AV nodal blockers
Emergency action plan if prolonged tachycardia
Letter to GP listing contraindicated medications
Electrophysiology appointment within 2-4 weeks

marking_criteria.item: Recognises short PR interval and delta wave on ECG
Correctly identifies WPW syndrome diagnosis
Lists contraindicated medications (digoxin, verapamil, diltiazem)
Explains risk of VF if AV nodal blockers used in AF with WPW
Recommends catheter ablation as definitive treatment
Considers bridging antiarrhythmic (flecainide) if symptomatic
Arranges urgent electrophysiology referral
Provides education on safe vagal manoeuvres
Documents medication contraindications prominently
Addresses occupational risk given healthcare role

learning_objectives: Identify ECG features of Wolff-Parkinson-White syndrome
Understand contraindicated medications in pre-excitation syndromes
Recognise catheter ablation as curative treatment for accessory pathways
Apply knowledge of re-entrant tachycardia mechanisms
references: eTG - Cardiovascular: Supraventricular tachycardia and pre-excitation
CSANZ Clinical Practice Update on SVT Management 2020
Emergency Medicine Australasia - WPW and AF management guidelines

osces.title: Pulmonary Embolism with RV Strain - Thrombolysis Decision

patient_scenario.chief_complaint: Severe dyspnoea and pleuritic chest pain after international flight, hypotensive in ED
patient_scenario.history_presenting_illness: Presented 2 hours after 14-hour flight from Los Angeles. Sudden onset severe dyspnoea while walking through airport, sharp right-sided pleuritic chest pain, near-syncope in taxi. Pain worse with deep inspiration, rated 8/10. Mild calf discomfort right leg noticed 2 days ago. On combined oral contraceptive pill for 10 years. No recent surgery or immobilisation apart from long flight. No haemoptysis. Sister had DVT age 35 during pregnancy.

social_history.occupation_detail: International flight attendant, frequent long-haul flights (2-3 per month)

patient_scenario.family_history: Sister DVT age 35 in pregnancy, maternal grandmother PE age 72, no known thrombophilia

examination_findings.cardiovascular: JVP elevated 6cm. Tachycardic, regular. Loud P2, right ventricular heave. No murmurs. Cool peripheries, delayed capillary refill.
examination_findings.respiratory: Tachypnoeic, using accessory muscles. Clear lung fields, no crackles or wheeze. Reduced air entry right base.
examination_findings.other_systems: Right calf 2cm larger than left, mild tenderness, no erythema. Alert but anxious, GCS 15.

investigations.ecg: Sinus tachycardia 118 bpm, S1Q3T3 pattern, T wave inversions V1-V4, incomplete RBBB, right axis deviation
investigations.chest_xray: Hampton's hump right lower zone (wedge-shaped opacity), prominent pulmonary artery, otherwise clear
investigations.bloods: D-dimer 4250 ng/mL (markedly elevated), Troponin I 145 ng/L (elevated), BNP 480 pg/mL, ABG (6L O2): pH 7.48, PaO2 68mmHg, PaCO2 28mmHg, HCO3 22, Lactate 3.2 mmol/L
investigations.echocardiogram: Bedside echo: Dilated RV with reduced function, RV:LV ratio 1.3, septal flattening, moderate TR, RVSP 55mmHg, McConnell's sign present (RV free wall hypokinesis with preserved apex)
investigations.other: CTPA: Large saddle PE with bilateral segmental emboli, RV:LV ratio 1.4, no contrast in right lower lobe artery. Doppler USS legs: Extensive right femoral and popliteal DVT

immediate: Urgent thrombolysis assessment - sPESI score 3 (high risk)
Alteplase 100mg IV over 2 hours after consent - not PBS listed
short_term: ICU admission for haemodynamic monitoring
Commence heparin infusion after thrombolysis completed
Transition to rivaroxaban 15mg BD for 21 days - PBS code 10293M
Cease oral contraceptive permanently
Serial echo to assess RV recovery
long_term: Continue rivaroxaban 20mg daily after initial 21 days
Duration minimum 6 months, consider indefinite (unprovoked + OCP)
Thrombophilia screening after anticoagulation completed
Alternative contraception counselling (Mirena IUD recommended)
Occupational assessment for flying fitness
discharge_planning: Discharge when RV function improved and stable on oral anticoagulation
Compression stockings for post-thrombotic syndrome prevention
Education on anticoagulation adherence and bleeding precautions
Respiratory physician follow-up for CTEPH surveillance

marking_criteria.item: Recognises submassive PE with RV strain on echo
Correctly calculates sPESI score indicating high risk
Recommends thrombolysis for haemodynamic instability
Screens for thrombolysis contraindications
Appropriate anticoagulation choice and dosing (rivaroxaban)
Identifies OCP as major risk factor requiring cessation
Plans appropriate anticoagulation duration (≥6 months)
Arranges ICU admission for monitoring
Considers thrombophilia testing after anticoagulation
Addresses occupational implications for flight attendant

learning_objectives: Risk stratify pulmonary embolism using sPESI score and RV dysfunction markers
Apply Australian guidelines for thrombolysis in submassive PE
Select appropriate anticoagulation regimen for PE treatment
Identify and modify risk factors for recurrent VTE
references: Thrombosis and Haemostasis Society of Australia and New Zealand PE guidelines 2023
Australian Commission on Safety and Quality in Health Care - VTE prevention guidelines
